Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, NO SENDS — every email path in tests is faked.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 7 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these; the test file is new):
  server/pipeline/orchestrator.py
  tests/test_stuck_unit_escalation.py

THE LIVE INCIDENT, measured on production today (2026-07-31) — this is not hypothetical, it is running
right now and has been for 15 days:

Episode `2026-06-24-conversation-with-allendalevis` (guest Nick Lillie) published 2026-07-16. Its
+7-day follow-up email has NEVER been sent. Instead, the VPS daily cron has retried it EVERY MORNING
for 15 consecutive days. Evidence:
  * /var/log/podcast-daily-cron.log shows one `{"action":"followup", "days_since_publish":N,
    "episode_id":"2026-06-24-conversation-with-allendalevis", "result":"promo-kit-sent"}` entry per day,
    with N walking 7, 8, 9 ... 15. Every day. No alarm anywhere, no escalation, no digest entry.
  * The episode's publish unit `promo_email:followup:<addr>` is
    {"state": "failed", "attempts": 4, "next_attempt_at": "2026-07-28T14:10:02Z", "receipt": null}.
    next_attempt_at is DAYS in the past and is not being honoured — the cron re-enters regardless.
  * The guest was NOT spammed: Gmail confirms only 3 legitimate messages ever reached that address.
    Every attempt was refused downstream. The damage is a missing follow-up plus 15 days of silence,
    not duplicate sends. Preserve that property: your fix must never make a stuck unit start sending.

WHY IT CAN NEVER SUCCEED (measured by executing the gate against production state):
  orchestrator's `_evaluate_publish_gate` returns eligible=False for this episode with failures
  including `readback_stale_or_missing` (plus transistor_not_public / youtube_main_not_public /
  site_show_notes_not_public, all of which are consequences of the same stale readback evidence).
  The episode IS genuinely public — Transistor, YouTube and the site were all verified live on
  2026-07-16 — but the PROOF expired, and nothing in the system ever refreshes it. So:
    handle_send_followup -> handle_send_promo_kit / publish-completion gate -> blocked
    -> stage stays `promo-kit-sent` -> tomorrow's cron sees stage promo-kit-sent and
       days_since_publish >= 7 -> retries -> forever.
  The gate being fail-closed is CORRECT and must not be weakened: it refuses to claim published
  without proof. The defects are that stale proof has no refresh path, and that a unit failing the
  same way N times produces no alarm.

FIX BOTH DEFECTS. Read the relevant code first: the daily-cron follow-up loop (search for
`days_since_publish >= 7`), `handle_send_followup`, `handle_send_promo_kit`, `_evaluate_publish_gate`,
`_queue_publish_incident`, and the publish-unit state helpers.

1. HONOUR BACKOFF AND CAP RETRIES. The daily cron must not re-enter a unit whose `next_attempt_at` is
   in the future, and must stop re-entering entirely once attempts reach a named cap constant
   (MAX_UNIT_ATTEMPTS, comment it with this incident). Attempts must actually INCREMENT and
   next_attempt_at must actually advance on each failure — exponential backoff from a named base, so
   a broken unit costs one attempt on day 1, then day 2, day 4, day 8, not 15 identical attempts.
2. ESCALATE INSTEAD OF SILENTLY RETRYING. When a unit reaches the cap, or when the same unit has been
   failing for more than a named number of days (STUCK_UNIT_ALERT_DAYS), queue an incident through the
   EXISTING `_queue_publish_incident` path with a kind like "unit-stuck", naming the episode, the unit,
   the attempt count, the days stuck, and the last failure reason. Do not invent a new alerting
   mechanism. After escalating, the cron records the unit as escalated and stops re-attempting it until
   a human/heal action resets it — a stuck unit must become LOUD and IDLE, never quiet and busy.
   Every cron pass must also record the skip in its `actions` list (result "skipped", reason naming
   backoff or escalation) so the daily log shows the truth instead of a fake retry.
3. DISTINGUISH STALE PROOF FROM NOT-PUBLISHED. `_evaluate_publish_gate` currently reports an episode
   whose readbacks went stale identically to one that was never published. Add that distinction to the
   verdict (e.g. a `stale_evidence` flag / a failure classification) WITHOUT weakening eligibility:
   stale evidence still blocks. Then, in the follow-up path, a block caused ONLY by stale/missing
   readback evidence must raise an incident that names refreshing the readback as the required action,
   rather than being indistinguishable from "this episode isn't public". Do NOT auto-refresh readbacks
   and do NOT auto-publish anything in this lane — surfacing the correct next action is the job.

TESTS (tests/test_stuck_unit_escalation.py; at least 7; fake email/dispatch, tmp episode dirs, fixed
`now`; read tests/test_publishing.py for the established fixture and fake patterns; NO network, NO real
sends):
 (1) THE REAL INCIDENT: an episode at stage promo-kit-sent, published 15 days ago, whose followup unit
     is {state failed, attempts 4, next_attempt_at in the past} -> running the daily cron queues a
     "unit-stuck" incident naming the unit and the days stuck, and does NOT attempt another send
     (assert the send fake was never called);
 (2) NEGATIVE: a unit whose next_attempt_at is in the FUTURE is not attempted, and the cron records a
     skip with a backoff reason (assert it appears in actions — a silent skip is the banned case);
 (3) attempts increment and next_attempt_at advances with exponential backoff across three simulated
     failures (assert the intervals grow);
 (4) NEGATIVE: once attempts reach MAX_UNIT_ATTEMPTS the unit is never attempted again and is marked
     escalated (assert the send fake call count stops growing across two more cron passes);
 (5) NEGATIVE: a healthy episode's follow-up still sends normally on day 7 — the guard must not break
     the working path (assert one send, exactly once, and not again on day 8);
 (6) the publish gate reports stale-evidence distinctly from never-published, and both remain
     INELIGIBLE (assert eligibility is unchanged — the fail-closed property is preserved);
 (7) NEGATIVE: a follow-up blocked solely by stale readback evidence queues an incident whose message
     names refreshing the readback, and still performs no send;
 (8) determinism: identical inputs and `now` produce identical actions and incidents.
Keep tests/test_publishing.py and tests/test_orchestrator.py green. Note that two publishing tests are
date-pinned and may already fail on some dates; do not "fix" them by changing production behaviour —
if one is red before your change, leave it and say so.
